Team — attaching first-pass RCA (nordicpay_rca_v1.pdf) and an initial remediation tracker (remediation_tracker_v1.xlsx). Highlights below; full technical write-up in the PDF.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: regression introduced by a batching optimization that was pushed as part of the 2026-07-09 throughput patch. For certain traffic patterns (short requests with interleaved large responses), the dynamic batch sizing heuristic selected overly-large batches which triggered internal queueing and kernel-level priority inversion on the GPU. This caused latency amplification under the specific NordicPay request mix.
- Impact: affected the settlement endpoint only (model variant stabled for short-latency configs). 5xx were caused by internal resource timeouts when the kernel queue exceeded retry windows. Estimated impacted traffic: 11–14% of requests during the window.
- Immediate mitigation applied: rolled back the dynamic batch heuristic at 07:34 UTC; applied a soft-rate cap to the settlement route; increased request retry window to prevent 5xx. These steps reduced errors and brought p99 back down within ~6 minutes.

Open corrective actions (from remediation_tracker_v1.xlsx):
1) Stabilize heuristic (owner: SRE - Dylan) — rework algorithm and add canary tests (due 2026-07-24).
2) Add route-level circuit breaker + SLA-aware fallback (owner: Platform - Sean) — design doc and rollout plan (due 2026-07-31).
3) Improve observability for per-route kernel queue depth (owner: Infra - Laura) — dashboard and alert thresholds (due 2026-07-21).
4) Customer-facing postmortem + credit recommendation (owner: Soojin) — draft for review (due 2026-07-17).

Attachments: nordicpay_rca_v1.pdf (RCA), remediation_tracker_v1.xlsx (action items). Also included relevant kernel traces excerpt and correlating traces (see attached notes in PDF).

I'll incorporate any feedback and move to a final RCA.
